purpose: Section 20: the ONE evidence-backed redesign permitted in this phase. Per 13/14's findings, the confusion evidence does not justify merging, splitting, or renaming any of the 12 taxonomy states (all remain product-actionable). It DOES justify a precise, minimal clarification to the OPERATIONAL RUBRIC's shared 'textual overlap with the claim's location' precondition, which was underspecified for two evidence-confirmed scenarios: composite/chapeau claims, and sibling-adjacent candidates. This artifact freezes that clarification as REPLACEMENT_RUBRIC_V2 before any re-adjudication occurs.
whyThisCountsAsTheOnePermittedRedesign: Section 19-20 frame the permitted redesign in terms of 'ontology simplification' with an illustrative example of splitting into orthogonal dimensions - but explicitly caveat that example as 'only illustrative, not to be adopted unless evidence-backed,' and require only that any replacement be 'the MINIMUM simplification the confusion data supports,' justified by confusion evidence, conceptual-overlap rationale, product-actionability rationale, and safety-information-preservation rationale. This clarification satisfies all four: it is directly derived from the confusion matrix (13), it identifies the TRUE locus of conceptual overlap (a shared precondition, not the state definitions themselves), it passed the product-actionability test in the negative (14 - no state should be merged), and it strictly preserves every safety distinction the original 12-state taxonomy encodes. Per this phase's single-redesign-only rule, this clarification consumes the one permitted attempt; if the holdout re-test below also fails the reproducibility gates, this phase concludes NEEDS_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION rather than attempting a second (state-count) redesign.
whatDidNotChange: All 12 state names and their conceptual definitions (unchanged from docs/evaluation-v2-iteration/02-state-taxonomy.json and 06-taxonomy-operational-rubric.json).
Every necessary/sufficient/exclusion condition NOT touched by the two new rules below.

The frozen Workstream A matcher, fingerprint policy, or algorithm version (evaluation-v2-algorithm.v3) - this redesign is confined entirely to the human/adjudicator-facing rubric text and touches zero production or evaluator-engine code.

newRule1_locationScopingForCompositeClai.name: LOCATION_SCOPING_RULE_FOR_COMPOSITE_CLAIMS
newRule1_locationScopingForCompositeClai.rule: When the ground-truth claim IS a chapeau/composite claim (an introductory/general-prohibition sentence of an enumerated list, or any claim whose own ground-truth unit is authored to span an entire enumerated family as a single combined claim rather than one specific enumerated sub-item), 'the claim's source location' for every DISCOVERY-layer necessary/exclusion condition above means ONLY: (a) text that directly quotes, closely paraphrases, or is structurally anchored at the chapeau/composite sentence's OWN span, OR (b) a candidate whose own self-reported scope explicitly addresses the general prohibition/permission AS A WHOLE, not merely one specific enumerated sub-item it introduces. A candidate, safety-flag, or verification finding anchored at a SPECIFIC enumerated sub-item beneath the chapeau does NOT by itself establish DISCOVERED_ONLY or DISCOVERED_REVIEW_REQUIRED for the chapeau's own claim - at most it establishes that SUB-ITEM's own separate discovery status, which is a different ground-truth unit's concern, not this one's.
newRule1_locationScopingForCompositeClai.evidenceBasis: 13-taxonomy-confusion-analysis.json's dominant cluster: 13 of 17 confused cases were isChapeauShape=True, and the adjudicators' own rationales show exactly this scoping question splitting them (Adjudicator B credited family-wide flags; Adjudicators A/C required the chapeau's own exact span).

newRule2_siblingAdjacencyForTextualOverl.name: SIBLING_ADJACENCY_RULE_FOR_TEXTUAL_OVERLAP
newRule2_siblingAdjacencyForTextualOverl.rule: A candidate whose own sectionRef names a DIFFERENT, sibling enumerated sub-item under the same parent section as the claim (the same structural sibling test the frozen I_CLAIM_IDENTITY dimension applies: same parent/base section, different top-level enumerated sub-item) does NOT count as 'textually overlapping the claim's own location' merely because its excerpt text is spatially adjacent to, or runs into, the claim's own source span. Overlap must be with the CLAIM'S OWN anchored span (or, for a composite/chapeau claim, per Rule 1 above) - not with a neighboring sibling provision's text.
newRule2_siblingAdjacencyForTextualOverl.evidenceBasis: 13-taxonomy-confusion-analysis.json's secondary finding on fwrg-6.06-b-ii: two of three adjudicators counted a sibling sub-clause's bleeding-adjacent excerpt as overlap; one did not.
newRule2_siblingAdjacencyForTextualOverl.relationToFrozenMatcher: This rule applies the ALREADY-FROZEN SAME_COVENANT_FAMILY_IS_NOT_SAME_SEMANTIC_CLAIM principle (Workstream A, Section 10, frozen in 05-matcher-freeze.json) to the DISCOVERY-layer rubric. It introduces no new principle into the evaluator's own code or matching policy - it only makes the reviewer-facing rubric consistent with a discipline the matcher already enforces. The frozen matcher itself is NOT modified by this artifact.
